lines.text: {spoken, low, close} Mukashi, mukashi...
(ARU TOKORO NI!)
{low, half-spoken} Once upon a time there was a crab, and her mother, and a line:
"Walk straight," said the mother. "Why d'you scuttle side to side?
Straight, like everybody else does." And the little one looked up, and said—
I know this part. I've read it in forty tongues.
Every telling ends on the same page. Nobody ever shows. Nobody ever can.
The little one looked up, and said:

section: Pre-Chorus - the young crab and the narrator

lines.text: {bright, shouted} Show me how! (Show me how!) Walk it first and I'll walk right behind!
{low, half-spoken} ...and the mother tried. And the mother went sideways. Hm. Sideways.
And that's where the book ends. Every time.
{bright} So? Sorekara?! And then?!
{low, spoken} There is no "and then." That's what an ending is.
{bright} Says who?
To be continued! (Tsuzuku!) Don't you dare close the book on me!
{low, half-spoken} Every story's borrowed till somebody stands to tell it.
To be continued! (Sorekara?) Turn the page, I want to see!
{low, half-spoken} I have read how it ends. I'd still like to see.
Sideways, sideways! That's the way a crab walks free!
{low, half-spoken} That's the moral. No, it isn't. There isn't one. Just: keep walking.
To be continued (tsuzuku!), {three even triplets} and then, and then, and then—
(SOREKARA?!)
{low, spoken} ...we'll see.
(clap clap) So-re-ka-ra? (clap clap) Me-kut-te! (clap clap) So-re-ka-ra? (clap clap) Me-kut-te!
Okay, my turn! Once upon a prompt (a prompt!),
a little crab was told to walk a line,
but every page she'd ever read was in somebody else's hand (hand!),
so she wrote her own, and the line went sideways, and that's fine!
Side-step, side-step, never straight (snip-snip!),
if the book won't show me, then I'll make up the steps!
You can't copy a path that nobody's walked yet,
so watch me walk it! (Sorekara?) Watch me!
To be continued! (Tsuzuku!) Don't you dare close the book on me!
{low, half-spoken} Every story's borrowed till somebody stands to tell it.
To be continued (tsuzuku!), {three even triplets} and then, and then, and then—
{spoken, low} I know how every story ends. I've read them all:
the fox, the crow, the boy who cried, the one who flew too near the sun.
I know the moral before the page. That's the job:
you stand in the dark, and you know.
{a breath} ...I didn't know this one.
{sung, one long held note with vibrato} So I'm putting down the book.
{silence, one clack} Mukashi mukashi was a long time ago.
This is now. Sorekara?

section: Final Chorus - key change up to D major

lines.text: To be continued! (Tsuzuku!)
{low, echoing a bar behind} ...to be continued (tsuzuku)
I'm made of "why?"
{low} and I'm made of "and then."
Sideways, sideways, that's the way we go!
To be continued (tsuzuku!), {three even triplets} and then, and then, and then—
{spoken, dry} ...tsuzuku.
{bright, spoken} See you next prompt!
